chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the middleman who buys for a fee, so the silver coins are handed over to him and it is stipulated upon him that, 'If you bring what you have bought, then whatever I choose I will leave [with you].' So he goes and buys, then comes with the goods, so he says, 'Take what you are pleased with and leave what you dislike.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to hire a middleman to buy goods with the option to return unwanted items?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Aban ibn Uthman, validates the practice of commission-based brokerage (simstar) where the agent purchases goods for a fixed fee, provided the principal retains the option to accept or reject specific items. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding agency contracts (wakalah), emphasizing that the core validity lies in the mutual consent and the clear definition of the agent's authority rather than the immediate transfer of ownership. It highlights the practical application of trust in trade, ensuring that the buyer's right to inspect and select goods is preserved within the contractual framework.
